bar: Bar chart showing counts for alpha, beta, gamma, delta, and epsilon, with delta having the highest count.
line-multi: Line chart showing series A and B over 24 hours; Series B consistently outperforms Series A.
scatter: Scatter plot showing groups P and Q; data suggests a positive correlation between x and y.
histogram: Histogram showing a right-skewed distribution with a peak around 45, indicating most values are clustered in this range.
boxplot: Box plot showing that group B has the highest value range compared to groups A and C.
stacked-bar: Stacked bar chart showing market share by region (North, South, West) across four quarters. North dominates Q2.
stacked-area: Stacked area chart showing varying series compositions over 24 hours, with S0 consistently dominating.
donut: Donut chart showing category proportions: alpha (30%), beta (35%), delta (15%), gamma (15%).
heatmap: Heatmap showing strong correlation between options A and C, with option D also exhibiting high positive correlations.
ecdf: Empirical cumulative distribution plot showing increasing proportions of x values up to approximately 90.
hexbin: Hexbin density plot showing high point concentration around x=5 and y=8.
kde2d-contour: 2D KDE shows two distinct density clusters in the data, suggesting a bimodal distribution.
beeswarm: Beeswarm plot showing groups A, B, and C with varying values; group B has the widest spread.
clustermap: Clustermap heatmap showing value correlations between s0 and various data points g0-g6.
quiver: Vector-field (quiver) plot: a grid of arrows whose length and darkness grow toward the right, showing increasing magnitude.
regression-ci-band: Scatter plot with regression line and confidence interval shows a positive correlation between x and y.
surface-3d: 3D surface plot showing maximum value at the apex.
imshow-interpolated: Gaussian blur heatmap showing two distinct blue concentrations.
streamplot: Streamplot of a vector field: curved streamlines with arrowheads converge and diverge, colored by speed on a blue ramp.
choropleth: Global exposure index map: Higher exposure is concentrated in Europe and North America, using quintile classes.
map-bivariate: Bivariate choropleth map showing global variation in two variables; high values concentrated in Europe and Asia.
map-bubble: Proportional-symbol world map: synthetic per-city values drawn as area-true blue bubbles, larger bubbles meaning larger values.
map-flow: Illustrative connection map: Great-circle links show increasing volume flow across the globe.
map-pie: Pie-glyph world map: a small multi-slice pie showing category shares placed at each world region.
map-bars: Bar-glyph world map: a small multi-bar chart placed at each world region.
map-tilegrid: Tile-grid cartogram: one equal-size rounded tile per country in a rough geographic layout, each shaded by its exposure quintile.
map-diverging: World map showing net change in synthetic demo data by country; Russia and United States gained significantly, while China lost.
map-small-multiples: Small-multiples world map: one panel per year from 2021 to 2024, the same quintile breaks throughout, with more countries shaded darker over time.
gaussian-process: Gaussian process regression: a bold posterior mean curve with a 95% credible band that widens away from the observations, faint posterior sample functions, and black observed points.
violin: Violin plot of three groups A, B and C: each a mirrored kernel-density shape on a shared value axis, colored red, orange and yellow.
